archetypes.name: signal-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a novel SIGTERM→SIGKILL kill-loop that reads an externally-written PID file; verify the kill-loop logic, PID reuse risk, and the 5-second grace window implementation before SIGKILL escalation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the new `larch_bm_signal_paired_pid` helper design in `scripts/breadcrumb-monitor.sh` against the plan spec: does the 32-byte read plus digit-only validation correctly reject empty strings, non-ASCII content, and multi-line PID files? Verify the kill-loop `kill -0` polling terminates after exactly 5 iterations (1-second sleep × 5) before escalating to SIGKILL, and that the plan's Bash 3.2 portability constraint (no namerefs, no mapfile) is honored in both the new helper and the kill-loop body. Check whether any Family B script (ship-pr.sh, ci-wait.sh, run-step5-review.sh, etc.) installs `trap '' TERM` or `trap ... TERM` that would silently absorb SIGTERM and defeat the grace-period poll. Confirm that `larch_quiet_write_paired_pid_file` in `scripts/lib-quiet.sh` uses an atomic mktemp+mv -f sequence and that the plan's test case for a SIGTERM-resistant process correctly exercises the SIGKILL escalation path rather than trivially passing because the test process exits on its own. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: callsite-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan updates 9 Family B scripts and roughly 12 SKILL.md fenced blocks; a specialist should verify the callsite list is exhaustive against current repo evidence and no Family B fence in orchestrator Markdown is silently omitted.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check the plan's enumerated Family B callsite list (ship-pr.sh, ci-wait.sh, run-step5-review.sh, review-and-fix.sh, run-step2-dispatch.sh, step2-implement.sh, collect-agent-results.sh, dispatch-with-waterfall.sh, dispatch-plan-voters.sh) against the nine-entry denylist enforced in `scripts/lint-foreground-markers.sh` to confirm the plan covers every existing denylist entry without additions or omissions. Scan every fenced block invoking a Family B script in `skills/design/SKILL.md`, `skills/implement/SKILL.md`, `skills/shared/external-reviewers.md`, `skills/shared/dialectic-protocol.md`, and all listed `skills/design/references/*.md` and `skills/research/references/*.md` files to verify each is explicitly named in the plan's SKILL.md update section. Check whether any `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` or `.claude/rules/*.md` files contain Family B fence blocks the plan silently omits, since those paths are part of the orchestrator-facing Markdown surface the linter will enforce after this PR lands. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: linter-invariant
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds two new lint enforcement tokens to lint-foreground-markers.sh; verify the linter logic, step-7a.sh carve-out justification, five-line look-back window semantics, and fixture coverage are mutually consistent.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan's `scripts/lint-foreground-markers.sh` update against `scripts/lint-foreground-markers.md` to confirm the new `has_pid_alloc` and `has_pid_flag` checks are documented with exact error wording and that the `step-7a.sh` carve-out rationale is justified by evidence in the existing denylist and its associated .md contract. Verify the four new fixture categories in `scripts/test-lint-foreground-markers.sh` (missing allocation, allocation-without-flag, both-present-pass, step-7a-foreground-pass) are sufficient to distinguish a correct linter from an off-by-one error on the five-line look-back window used by both the existing per-anchor comment rule and the new checks. Check whether the plan's requirement to use `case` statements over the 9-entry list is realistic given the existing loop structure near line 345 of `lint-foreground-markers.sh`, and whether any existing fixture would spuriously fail if the new checks are evaluated before the `step-7a.sh` branch guard. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
